summary: Hostile audit #16 — the learning CONSUMERS: estimator, history_store, services

survived.title: Confidence breakpoint table has a dead band at 0.79–0.80; the best-learned rooms fall through it and render as LOW / red "error"
survived.mechanism:
_BREAKPOINTS (lines 117-139) declares MEDIUM as max_score=0.79 and HIGH as min_score=0.80. _breakpoint_for_score uses an INCLUSIVE double-sided test `bp["min_score"] <= score <= bp["max_score"]`, so any score strictly between 0.79 and 0.80 matches NO bucket and hits the fall-through `return dict(_BREAKPOINTS[-1])` — which is the LOW entry (ui_rank 1, ui_variant "error").

That band is exactly where the best real rooms land. _score_room_confidence caps at base 0.55 + sample_bonus 0.25 = 0.80, and the variance penalty is min(cv/0.5,1.0)*0.25. So a room with >=10 samples and a coefficient of variation under 2% scores in (0.79, 0.80).

PROVEN (executed against the real constants): room with 12 timing samples, avg_minutes 10.0, minutes_stddev 0.15 (9 seconds of spread — an exceptionally consistent room), zero accuracy drift:
  cv = 0.15/10.0 = 0.015 ; variance_penalty = (0.015/0.5)*0.25 = 0.0075
  score = 0.55 + 0.25 - 0.0075 = 0.7925
  _breakpoint_for_score(0.7925): high 0.80<=0.7925 FALSE; medium 0.7925<=0.79 FALSE; low 0.7925<=0.49 FALSE -> fall-through -> LOW / ui_rank 1 / ui_variant "error".

The full sweep at 12 samples / avg 10.0:
  stddev 0.00 -> 0.8000 -> high/success
  stddev 0.05 -> 0.7975 -> LOW/error
  stddev 0.10 -> 0.7950 -> LOW/error
  stddev 0.15 -> 0.7925 -> LOW/error
  stddev 0.20 -> 0.7900 -> medium/warning
  stddev 0.50 -> 0.7750 -> medium/warning

The ordering is INVERTED: the noisier room (stddev 0.50) renders amber "warning" while the tighter room (stddev 0.15) renders red "error". Job confidence is min(room scores) (line 983), so one such room drags the WHOLE job estimate into the red band.

src/renderers/learning.js:534 reads `breakpoint.ui_variant` straight into the chip colour and src/renderers/rooms.js:742 / 1196 do the same, so the red chip reaches the user verbatim.
survived.user_impact: The single most reliably-learned room in the house is badged red "Low confidence" on the card, and drags the whole job estimate to red with it — while a demonstrably worse-learned room next to it shows amber "Medium". Users are trained to distrust exactly the numbers they should trust, and the learning system appears not to be working after dozens of successful runs.
survived.guards_checked: _confidence_result (line 172) clamps and rounds to 4 dp before the lookup — round(0.7925,4)=0.7925, so rounding does not rescue it. The fall-through at line 167 is the only safety net and it returns the WRONG end of the table (_BREAKPOINTS[-1] is LOW, not the nearest tier). The mirror gap at (0.49, 0.50) is harmless only by accident — it also falls through to LOW, which happens to be correct there. tests/unit/test_learning_estimator.py [LE-1] parametrises exactly 0.79 and 0.80 and never a value in between, so the band is untested. No caller re-derives the label from confidence_score; the card trusts confidence_label / ui_variant.

survived.title: App-started (external) runs contribute battery=0.0 samples; the estimator consumes a learned 0.0 as a real number and derives battery_warning / mid_job_recharge_risk = False from it
survived.mechanism:
learning/external_ingest.py:1056-1105 (build_graduated_job) constructs the completed_job record with NO `battery` block at all — I read the whole literal; grep for "battery" in external_ingest.py returns zero hits. external_run.py:509 saves that record verbatim and immediately rebuilds stats. outcome.status is "completed" and used_for_learning is True (external_ingest.py:1084), so history_store.is_learning_job (line 414-428) admits it.

In the rebuilder, `total_battery_used = _safe_float(job.get("battery", {}).get("used"), 0.0)` -> 0.0, per_room_battery -> 0.0, and that 0.0 is accumulated into the SAME room_stats bucket as dispatched runs, diluting avg_battery_used toward zero.

The estimator then does `battery = _safe_float(match.get("avg_battery_used"), _DEFAULT_BATTERY_PER_ROOM)`. _safe_float (utils.py:20) only substitutes the default for None/""/"unknown"/"unavailable" — **0.0 is a valid float and passes straight through**. There is no zero-floor, no `area_sample_count`-style `battery_sample_count`, and no `source` marker distinguishing "learned 0%" from "no battery data".

PROVEN. Room bucket = 3 external samples (0.0 each) + 1 dispatched sample (8.0%): avg_battery_used = (0+0+0+8)/4 = 2.0. Five-room job, current_battery 25%, reserve 5%:
  total_battery_used            = 5 * 2.0 = 10.0   (truth ~5 * 8 = 40)
  required_start_battery        = 15.0
  battery_shortfall             = max(15-25, 0) = 0.0  -> battery_warning = False
  mid_job_recharge_needed       = max(10-25, 0) = 0.0  -> mid_job_recharge_risk = False
  remaining_battery_after_job   = 25 - 10 = +15%       (truth -15%)
  projected_recharge_overhead   = 10 * 0.05 = 0.5 min  (truth ~2.0 min)

With an all-external archive (the population external ingest exists to serve) avg_battery_used = 0.0 exactly: total_battery_used = 0.0, remaining_battery_after_job = current_battery, and the card asserts the job costs ZERO battery with battery_warning False at any charge level.

Critically, none of these outputs carry the confidence signal: confidence_score is computed from TIMING samples only (sample_count / minutes_stddev, lines 848-878). battery_warning and mid_job_recharge_risk are bare booleans presented as fact.
survived.user_impact: The card tells the user a 5-room job will finish with 15% left and shows no battery warning and no mid-job-recharge risk, when the job actually needs 40% and the robot will strand and dock mid-run. A user who mostly starts runs from the vendor app — precisely the user external ingest was built for — gets a battery model that converges on "this job is free".

survived.title: _find_room_match Pass 1 can NEVER match a Roborock room: it compares the raw "" intensity against the rebuilder's normalized "standard", so every Roborock room takes a permanent -0.15 intensity-mismatch penalty
survived.mechanism:
Roborock declares no clean_intensity axis at all (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:107-109: "clean_intensity is OMITTED from every profile on purpose"; rooms/room_defaults.py:45-47 documents the same). So rooms/room_manager.py:103 stores `clean_intensity=str(_default("clean_intensity", ""))` -> the literal empty string on EVERY Roborock room.

The two sides then normalize that empty string DIFFERENTLY:
  learning/manager.py:2201 (estimator projection): `str(room.get("clean_intensity","standard")).strip().lower()` -> ""
  learning/stats_rebuilder.py:477-479 (stats key):   `str(room.get("clean_intensity","standard")).strip().lower() or "standard"` -> "standard"

_find_room_match._intensity (line 476) does `str(item.get("clean_intensity","standard")).strip().lower() == clean_intensity` -> "standard" == "" -> **False, always**. Pass 1 is dead for every Roborock room. Pass 2 (line 484, ignore intensity) then matches and returns `(item, True)` -> intensity_mismatch=True -> a flat -0.15 subtracted at line 312, forever, on a bucket that is in fact an EXACT match.

This is the centralize-the-question failure: utils._room_key does `str(clean_intensity or 'standard')` (utils.py:171) — the same `or 'standard'` fold the rebuilder uses — so the ACCURACY lookup at line 854 aligns correctly. Only _find_room_match hand-rolls its own comparison and diverges.

PROVEN (executed). Roborock kitchen, 4 timing samples, avg 10.0 min, stddev 2.0:
  correct (no mismatch): 0.55 + 0.10 - 0.10 = 0.5500 -> medium / "warning"
  actual  (mismatch):    0.5500 - 0.15    = 0.4000 -> LOW / "error"
At 6 samples: 0.60 -> medium/warning becomes 0.45 -> LOW/error.

Job confidence is min(room scores) (line 983), so every Roborock job inherits the depressed score.
survived.user_impact: Roborock users see their room and job estimates permanently badged one confidence tier lower — often red "Low" instead of amber "Medium" — no matter how many clean runs they accumulate, because the estimator believes it is reading data from a different clean-intensity setting that Roborock does not even have.
survived.guards_checked: No caller normalizes clean_intensity before estimate(); learning/manager.py:2201 is the only projection and it preserves "". The dict.get default at line 476 does not fire — the key is PRESENT with value "standard" on the stats side and PRESENT with value "" on the request side. _room_key (line 854) folds ""->"standard" so the accuracy path is unaffected and does not surface the divergence. Eufy is unaffected: its clean_intensity_options are "Quick"/"Narrow"/"Deep" (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:421-425), all non-empty, so the `or "standard"` branch never fires there. Any future brand that omits the intensity axis inherits the same bug.

survived.title: Estimate consumes avg_minutes with no outlier rejection and no band check, and a single poisoned sample scores MEDIUM confidence because stddev of one sample is 0 by construction
survived.mechanism:
`minutes = _safe_float(match.get("avg_minutes"), _DEFAULT_ROOM_MINUTES)` takes the unweighted arithmetic mean straight through. The room_stats record ALSO carries minutes_min, minutes_max and partial_excluded_count — I grepped: the estimator, core/manager.py and every src/renderers/ file read NONE of them. The outlier band is computed and then discarded, so the estimator has no way to notice that its mean is unrepresentative.

This campaign has proven the archive contains rooms credited with a whole multi-room group's time. Two cases:

(a) n=3, samples 12 / 14 / 900 minutes (the poisoned room[0] credit):
    avg_minutes = 926/3 = 308.67 -> the card shows a 5h09m room and a job ETA anchored on it, against a true ~13 min.
    stddev = 418.1, cv = 1.354 -> full 0.25 variance penalty -> score 0.55 + 0.075 - 0.25 = 0.375 -> LOW.
    The confidence is correctly LOW but the NUMBER — the ETA, the job_eta_at wall-clock, the mop-wash cycle count, the dust-empty overhead — is 24x wrong and is presented as the estimate.

(b) n=1, a single 900-minute sample — the dangerous case:
    stats_rebuilder._stddev returns 0.0 for n<2, so minutes_stddev = 0.0.
    _score_room_confidence line 306 guards the variance penalty on `minutes_stddev > 0`, so variance_penalty = 0.0.
    score = 0.55 + min(1/10,1)*0.25 = 0.5750 -> _breakpoint_for_score -> **MEDIUM / ui_variant "warning"**.
    The card shows a 15-hour room at MEDIUM confidence from one unvalidated sample.

The model structurally rewards ignorance: zero variance is scored as perfect agreement, and n=1 always has zero variance.
survived.user_impact: A single bad archived run — one multi-room phase that credited the group's whole time to room[0] — moves the displayed job ETA by an order of magnitude, and when it is the room's FIRST run it does so under an amber "Medium confidence" badge. The user plans around a 15-hour ETA, or writes the feature off as broken.

It also keeps every sample whose paired area is None. At n>=4 with per-room area capture the gate does catch an inflated-area room[0] credit — but n=1 and n=3 are exactly the cold-start window where one bad sample defines the baseline. utils.evaluate_idle_wall_hold only holds runs with an unexplained >=20 min idle gap and steps aside entirely when had_errors or had_break_phase, so a group-credited room[0] with a legitimate error flag passes it. timing_sample_count reaches the estimator (line 848) but is used only for the confidence bonus, never as a minimum-samples floor on whether to use the match at all.

survived.title: HIGH confidence is mathematically unreachable for any real room, yet _learning_velocity reports runs_to_high=0 at 10 samples and runs_to_medium=0 always
survived.mechanism:
_score_room_confidence maxes at base 0.55 + sample_bonus 0.25 = 0.80, and the HIGH breakpoint min_score is 0.80. Reaching it requires sample_count >= 10 AND variance_penalty == 0 AND intensity_penalty == 0 AND accuracy_penalty == 0. variance_penalty is zero only when minutes_stddev <= 0 (line 306), and stats_rebuilder._stddev returns non-zero for any 10 wall-clock durations that are not byte-identical floats. accuracy_penalty is non-zero for any room that has ever been estimated and completed (any mean_abs_pct_error > 0 subtracts). So for a genuinely well-learned room the score asymptotes just BELOW 0.80 — which, per EST-1, is the dead band that renders red.

Meanwhile _SAMPLES_FOR_HIGH = ceil((0.80-0.55)/0.25*10) = ceil(10.0) = 10, and _learning_velocity returns `runs_to_high = max(10 - sample_count, 0)`. At sample_count=10 that is 0 — the card stops saying "N more runs" and implies the tier is reached — while current_tier is still "medium" (or red, per EST-1).

_SAMPLES_FOR_MEDIUM = ceil((0.50-0.55)/0.25*10) = ceil(-2.0) = -2, so `runs_to_medium = max(-2 - n, 0)` is **0 for every possible sample_count, including 0**. A brand-new unlearned room (source="default", score 0.20, tier LOW) is told it needs 0 more runs to reach MEDIUM.

The docstring at lines 142-144 concedes the targets are computed "assuming zero variance and no penalties" — but src/renderers/learning.js:615 and src/renderers/room-estimate.js:48 render runs_to_high as a user-facing promise, and the card falls silent once it hits 0.
survived.user_impact: The card advertises a HIGH/green confidence tier that no room can ever reach, counts the user down to it over ten runs, then reports "0 runs remaining" while the badge stays amber or red. An unlearned room is simultaneously scored LOW and told it needs zero more runs to be reliable. The learning-velocity feature actively misinforms.
survived.guards_checked: _learning_velocity clamps with max(...,0) but never cross-checks current_score against the tier it is counting toward — it returns current_tier alongside a contradictory runs_to_* of 0 with no reconciliation. Nothing recomputes the targets from the live penalties. tests/unit/test_learning_estimator.py [LE-8]/[LE-9] assert runs_to_high == 0 at saturation and > 0 at zero samples, which locks the behaviour in rather than catching it; no test asserts runs_to_medium.
confirmations: The arithmetic is exact and damning: _SAMPLES_FOR_MEDIUM = ceil((0.50-0.55)/0.25*10) = ceil(-2.0) = -2, so runs_to_medium = max(-2 - n, 0) is 0 for every n including 0 — a brand-new default-source room (score 0.20, LOW) is told it needs zero runs. _SAMPLES_FOR_HIGH = 10 and runs_to_high hits 0 at n=10 while HIGH needs score >= 0.80, which requires variance_penalty == 0 (i.e. minutes_stddev exactly 0). SEVERITY CORRECTED down: I refuted two of the finder's supporting claims. HIGH is NOT 'mathematically unreachable' — 0.80 is attainable when _stddev rounds to 0.0 with no drift/intensity penalty, so the claim is practical, not mathematical. And I grepped src/: runs_to_medium has NO renderer at all (only runs_to_high appears, at learning.js:615 and room-estimate.js:48, and only when > 0). So the always-zero runs_to_medium is latent payload junk, and the user-visible part is the card merely falling silent at n=10 — an absent promise, not a wrong number.

Both arithmetic claims verified against the source constants. _SAMPLES_FOR_MEDIUM = ceil((0.50-0.55)/0.25*10) = ceil(-2.0) = -2, so runs_to_medium = max(-2 - n, 0) = 0 for every n including 0 - an unlearned room (source='default', 0.20, LOW) is told it needs 0 more runs to reach MEDIUM. _SAMPLES_FOR_HIGH = ceil(10.0) = 10, so runs_to_high hits 0 at exactly 10 samples. HIGH unreachability confirmed: max is base 0.55 + sample_bonus 0.25 = 0.80, and the high bucket's min_score is 0.80, so it needs variance_penalty == 0, which per :306 requires minutes_stddev <= 0, which _stddev only returns for n<2 or byte-identical samples - contradicting the >=10-sample requirement. Renderers confirmed to surface runs_to_high as a countdown (src/renderers/learning.js:615, room-estimate.js:48) and to fall silent at 0.

survived.title: _find_room_match relaxed passes return the lexicographically-first bucket and ignore sample_count entirely — a 1-sample bucket beats a 30-sample one
survived.mechanism:
Passes 2-5 iterate `room_stats` and `return item` on the FIRST structural match. room_stats arrives in stats_rebuilder order: `for key in sorted(room_stats.keys())` (line 623) where the key is `map_id::slug::mode::clean_times::is_carpet::clean_intensity::edge_mopping` — a plain lexicographic string sort. Neither sample_count nor timing_sample_count is consulted anywhere in _find_room_match, and there is no blending across the relaxed dimension.

survived.title: A single transient read failure makes record_estimate_accuracy silently overwrite the entire accuracy history with one job's rooms
survived.mechanism: `existing = copy.deepcopy(self.store.load_accuracy_stats(...) or {})` cannot distinguish "no history yet" from "history exists but could not be read". history_store.read_json (157-178) catches `except Exception` on ANY failure — OSError on the SMB-mounted config share, permission error, partial read — logs it and returns None; load_accuracy_stats (565-579) maps that to None and caches the None. record_estimate_accuracy then builds `rooms_data = existing.get("rooms", {})` = {} and, at 655-664, UNCONDITIONALLY calls save_accuracy_stats with `{"rooms": rooms_data}` — write_json does an atomic os.replace, not a merge. The prior file is gone. The write side of exactly this hazard is reasoned about in this function's own comment ("a write_json failure (it re-raises, e.g. on an SMB hiccup)") and in write_json's docstring ("the failure mode that left `Extra data` trailing bytes on the SMB-mounted config share"); the read side is unguarded. Worse, the save happens even when `recorded` is empty — a failed read plus a job whose rooms carry no snapshot estimate writes `{"rooms": {}}`, a total wipe for zero gain.
survived.user_impact: Concrete: store holds 14 room keys / 60 graded samples; one OSError while reading learned/accuracy_stats.json during a 2-room job's finalize rewrites the file with 2 keys at sample_count 1. survived.title: A failed or absent read is cached as None for the life of the process, and load_*_stats has no bypass — so _reload_learning_stats_now's documented "guarantees the current on-disk stats" is false

The lookup is `if key in cache: return cache[key]` — membership, not truthiness — so a cached None is a permanent answer. survived.title: write_json is rename-atomic but not durable — no fsync before os.replace, so a power loss can leave a zero-length learned file that read_json then reports as "no data"
survived.mechanism: The temp file is written through os.fdopen and closed by the `with` block, which flushes to the OS but never calls os.fsync(fd); os.replace then renames. The rename is ordered but the DATA is not: after a power cut or a hard host reset the directory entry can be visible while the file's blocks are still unflushed, leaving a zero-length or short room_stats.json / trouble_rooms.json. read_json then hits `if not raw: return None` (line 163) or a JSONDecodeError, both of which return None — feeding IO-2's overwrite cascade and IO-3's negative cache. The docstring (181-187) claims the design means "a reader (or a restart mid-write) never sees a half-written or doubly-written file", which is true for a graceful restart and for a concurrent reader, but is not true for an ungraceful power loss — the claim is broader than what the code delivers.
survived.user_impact: A power cut during a stats write can leave the learned file empty; on the next run the integration reports no learned history rather than an error, and the trouble-rooms accumulator then overwrites what remains (IO-2).

survived.mechanism: `completed_room_ids` is only ever appended by a ROOM ROLLOVER, and both brands' rollovers structurally refuse to roll the last room: the Eufy/sequential path returns early at `jobs/active_job.py:970` (`if current_index >= len(unresolved_room_ids) - 1: return active_job`), and its counter-plateau branch carries the comment "expected_rooms caps boundaries at N-1, so this never rolls the final room"; the Roborock native path (`jobs/active_job.py:1238`) completes a room only when the device reports a DIFFERENT target, which never happens for the last one. The stranded-run reaper (`listeners/pause_timeout.py:114-122` → `async_finalize_stranded_job`, `forced_outcome_status="interrupted"`) exists precisely for the case where the robot ALREADY finished and docked but no completion packet arrived (the documented Eufy MQTT push-only staleness) — the one case where the last room definitely WAS cleaned.
